summary: Croatia has been a full Schengen Area member since January 2023: EU and EFTA citizens enter freely, around 60 visa-exempt nationalities can stay 90 days in any 180-day period (the ETIAS travel authorization is not yet in operation), and everyone else needs a Schengen short-stay visa costing €90.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area: Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs says third-country nationals, whether or not they need a visa, may stay up to 90 days in any 180-day period, and that time spent in Croatia is added to time spent in the other Schengen states. The remaining days can be checked with the EU's Entry/Exit System (EES) web tool.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs of Croatia — Visas (calculating time spent in the Schengen area)

fee.notes: Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs waives the fee for children up to 12, close family members of Croatian citizens, family members of EEA and Swiss citizens travelling with them, pupils, students and accompanying teachers travelling to study, and researchers; the Visa Code otherwise sets €45 for children aged 6–11. Fee set EU-wide since June 11, 2024.

source.name: Visa Code (Regulation (EC) No 810/2009), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 establishing a Community Code on Visas, Article 16(1) (visa fee), Article 1(1) (stays not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period) and Article 24(1) (a visa may be issued for one, two or multiple entries; validity up to five years, set on examination of each application), consolidated to 11 June 2024

applyWindow.text: The EU Visa Code says an application is lodged no more than six months before the start of the visit and, as a rule, no later than 15 calendar days before it; in justified urgent cases the consulate may accept it later.

source.name: EU Visa Code — Regulation (EC) No 810/2009, Article 9(1) (consolidated text)

visaTypes.name: Schengen Short-Stay Visa (Type C), single entry for Russian nationals

fee.notes: Standard fee under the Visa Code (Article 16): children aged 6 to 11 pay €45 and children under 6 pay nothing. The EU–Russia visa facilitation agreement is fully suspended (Council Decision (EU) 2022/1500), so its reduced fee does not apply.

source.name: European Commission — Daily News 7 November 2025: the EU adopts stricter rules on visas for Russian nationals (no more multiple-entry visas)
source.instrument: Commission rules on visas for Russian nationals adopted 7 November 2025, following approval by all Member States in the Visa Committee

applyWindow.text: The EU Visa Code says an application is lodged no more than six months before the start of the visit and, as a rule, no later than 15 calendar days before it; in justified urgent cases the consulate may accept it later.

source.name: EU Visa Code — Regulation (EC) No 810/2009, Article 9(1) (consolidated text)

visaTypes.name: Long-Stay Visa (Type D) / Temporary Stay Permit

fee.notes: Long-stay (D) visa fee, charged when you apply; a VFS Global service fee is added if you apply at a visa centre. The D visa is an entry visa for third-country nationals already granted temporary stay (or a stay-and-work permit): valid up to six months for one or more entries, it allows up to 30 days in Croatia, within which you register with the police and collect the biometric residence permit.

source.name: Croatian Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs — Visa fees (Pristojbe)

fee.notes: No D-visa fee for third-country nationals granted temporary stay to study, for secondary education or research. The D visa is an entry visa for third-country nationals already granted temporary stay (or a stay-and-work permit): valid up to six months for one or more entries, it allows up to 30 days in Croatia, within which you register with the police and collect the biometric residence permit.

source.name: Croatian Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs — Visa fees (Pristojbe)

fee.notes: Long-stay (D) visa fee for holders of a stay-and-work permit; a VFS Global service fee is added at a visa centre. The D visa is an entry visa for third-country nationals already granted temporary stay (or a stay-and-work permit): valid up to six months for one or more entries, it allows up to 30 days in Croatia, within which you register with the police and collect the biometric residence permit.

source.name: Croatian Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs — Visa fees (Pristojbe)

passportValidity.text: Non-EU passports must be valid for at least 3 months beyond your planned departure from the Schengen Area and have been issued within the last 10 years.

source.name: Croatian Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs — Documents for a Schengen visa application
source.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/399 (Schengen Borders Code), Article 6(1)(a); Regulation (EC) No 810/2009 (Visa Code), Article 12

source.name: Croatian Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs — Documents for a Schengen visa application

travelInsurance.text: Schengen visa applicants must hold travel medical insurance covering at least €30,000, valid across the Schengen Area for the whole stay. No official source we could read requires insurance of visa-exempt visitors; the UK government says British travellers may be asked to show proof of travel insurance at Croatian border control.

declarations.name: EES — Entry/Exit System (biometric registration)
declarations.submitWindow: At the border on first entry
declarations.text: Non-EU travelers are registered biometrically (fingerprints and photo) in the EU Entry/Exit System at Schengen external borders. Registration happens at the border. There is no mandatory advance step; where a self-service kiosk or a national app is offered, some data can be pre-registered to speed things up.

declarations.name: ETIAS — European Travel Information and Authorization System

fee.notes: Free for under-18s and over-70s. Valid 3 years or until passport expiry.

declarations.text: Visa-exempt travelers will need an ETIAS travel authorization to enter the Schengen Area. It is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch.

currencyLimits.text: Cash of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) must be declared when entering or leaving the EU.

notes: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU's Your Europe portal lists duty-free allowances of 1 litre of spirits (or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine), 4 litres of still wine, 16 litres of beer and other goods worth up to €300 (€430 by air or sea). For tobacco, Croatia applies the lower limit of 40 cigarettes to travellers arriving by land or sea; the higher limit is 200 cigarettes.
Between EU countries, alcohol and tobacco bought for your own use and not for resale carry no further duty, but customs can check the quantities against guideline levels, according to Your Europe.

payments.text: No official source we could read describes card acceptance in Croatia. Croatia's currency has been the euro since 2023, according to the European Central Bank.

safety.text: The UK government's travel advice says crime levels are low and violent crime is rare, and that pickpockets operate in tourist areas.

tips.text: The 90-day limit counts across the entire Schengen Area, not just Croatia: Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs says time spent in Croatia is added to time spent in the other Schengen states.

The UK government's travel advice says EES registration may take each passenger extra time, so be prepared to wait longer than usual at the border and allow more time for immigration controls when you leave the Schengen area.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Croatia?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders can visit Croatia and the rest of the Schengen Area visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS becomes mandatory, they will need to obtain this online authorization (€20) before travel.

faq.question: Is Croatia in the Schengen Area and does it use the euro?
faq.answer: Yes to both. Croatia joined the Schengen Area and adopted the euro on January 1, 2023, so prices are in euros and there are normally no border checks when arriving from other Schengen countries. Checks can still happen: the UK government's travel advice says there are checks at Slovenia's borders with Croatia, and Canada's says Schengen states may temporarily reintroduce internal border controls.

faq.question: How much does a Croatia Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The Schengen short-stay visa costs €90 for adults; Croatia's Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs waives the fee for children up to 12. It allows stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period across all Schengen countries, and applications are decided within 15 calendar days, extendable to 45.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Croatia?
faq.answer: ETIAS for visa-exempt travelers is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. Once in operation, the €20 travel authorization will be required for visa-exempt travelers to enter.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Croatia without a visa?
faq.answer: Visa-exempt non-EU visitors can stay up to 90 days within any 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area.
